problem:
Given that $\lambda =0$ and $\lambda =10$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$
worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=-2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -4 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}-8{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=4,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
